label: Hollow tubes save material at fixed bending stiffness; light-core optimum k² = 1 − q
notation: A = \sqrt{4\pi I}\,\sqrt{\tfrac{1-k^2}{1+k^2}} \text{ strictly decreasing in } k; \quad \mu'(k) = 0 \iff k^2 = 1 - q, \; 0 < q < 1
assumptions: Circular tube, outer radius R > 0, inner radius kR with 0 ≤ k < 1; bending stiffness measured by the second moment I = (π/4) R⁴ (1 − k⁴), held fixed; wall density ρ, core density qρ (q = 0 for a gas-filled core); local buckling as the symbolic bound t/R = 1 − k ≥ λ with λ = Cσ/E, 0 < λ ≤ 1.
scope_note: Proves that at fixed stiffness the wall area √(4πI)·√((1−k²)/(1+k²)) falls strictly with k, so a weightless core has no interior optimum; with core density ratio q the mass factor has μ'(k) = 2k(k² − (1−q))/(1−k⁴)^{3/2}, an interior critical point exists iff 0 < q < 1, and k* = √(1−q) is then the unique minimum (μ = √(q(2−q))); q ≥ 1 favours the solid rod; under the buckling bound the optimum is min(k*, 1−λ). Whether bird wing bones, quills and stems sit at these optima, and the value of C, are left to measurement.

label: Femoral wall thickness follows the bending-moment distribution along the shaft
notation: wall thickness t(x) \propto bending moment M(x), maximal at mid-shaft
reason: Already formalized in ThompsonLaws.Mechanics (uniformStressThickness); this module studies the cross-section at one station and does not restate the thickness–moment law.
